title: Levels of analysis, methods, and interpretative limits
rows: Cellular and molecular
Which cellular or molecular processes are being examined?
Cell culture, molecular assays, genetics, animal models
Mechanistic evidence requires caution when applied to an individual.
Circuit and systems
How are the relevant processes organised across circuits and systems?
Imaging, electrophysiology, lesion evidence, task performance
Regional activation is not a diagnosis.
Endocrine and immune
How are measured responses related to bodily regulation?
Hormone and immune assays; repeated sampling
Timing, health, medication, sleep, and assay variation affect results.
Behaviour and function
How are observed responses related to daily functioning?
Interviews, questionnaires, behavioural tasks, records
Symptom measures require interpretation alongside function and meaning.
Social context and implementation
How does application vary across settings?
Qualitative and mixed-methods research; implementation and policy evaluation
Resources, culture, law, and unequal access shape application.
note: Adapted editorially from original PDF pages 130–131. Questions have been clarified without adding measurements or findings; author approval is required. No single row provides a complete explanation.

title: Professional applications and quality safeguards
rows: Clinical services
What action may improve safety or functioning?
Collaborative assessment; outcome monitoring
Avoid unsupported biological testing and deterministic explanations.
Education
What support may improve participation and learning?
Observation, consultation, accessible teaching
Do not infer trauma or diagnosis from behaviour alone.
Healthcare
How can care reduce avoidable threat and improve continuity?
Medical review, communication, referral, quality data
Protect consent, privacy, and appropriate professional scope.
Government
Which population-level action has evidence and resources?
Surveillance, programme evaluation, policy analysis
Examine fairness, opportunity costs, and unintended harm.
Organisations
How can exposure management and recovery support improve?
Risk assessment, confidential referral, workforce indicators
Do not substitute individual training for safer systems.
note: Adapted editorially from original PDF pages 131–132. These are questions for planning and appraisal, not demonstrated intervention effects.
